You are an impartial replication auditor. A paper (OSTI 3365789, Geng et al., "Parallel-in-Time Solution of Allen-Cahn Equations by Integrating Operator Learning into the Parareal Method", J Sci Comput 2026) makes these core reproducible claims:

C1 (fine scheme accuracy): The Crank-Nicolson + finite-difference fine solver for the classical Allen-Cahn eq (u_t = eps^2 Lap u + u - u^3, periodic) is second-order accurate in space and time.
C2 (MBP): The classical AC solution obeys the Maximum Bound Principle, staying in [-1,1].
C3 (energy dissipation): The discrete energy functional E(u)=int(eps^2/2 |grad u|^2 + (u^2-1)^2/4) is non-increasing in time.
C4 (Parareal correctness+convergence): Parareal (Eq 13-14) with this fine solver (a) has the exact invariant that after k iterations the first k coarse intervals match the sequential fine solution, and (b) converges: ||U^k - U^{k-1}||_inf -> 0 and the Parareal solution converges to the sequential fine solution.
C5 (paper Sec 4.2.3): A NUMERICAL Crank-Nicolson coarse propagator (large coarse step dt=0.1) makes Parareal for AC slow/stagnating/MBP-violating (esp. for random ICs), motivating their CNN coarse propagator.

An independent reimplementation (CN+FFT-exact Helmholtz solve, full Picard convergence, merging-bubbles IC per paper Eq16 and random IC, eps=0.01, dt_coarse=0.1, dt_fine=0.001) produced these results (all numbers generated independently):

Notes: V1b spatial order used a smooth manufactured solution to isolate spatial order. C4C5 = merging bubbles; C5b = random IC. In both Parareal runs the NUMERICAL coarse propagator converged to the fine solution at ~1e-15 in ~10 iterations with no MBP violation.

For EACH claim C1..C5, judge: is it REPRODUCED, PARTIALLY reproduced, NOT reproduced, or CONTRADICTED by these independent results? Give a one-sentence justification each. Then give an OVERALL verdict from {REPLICATED, PARTIAL, SPOT-CHECK, CONTRADICTED, NO-GO} with a 2-sentence rationale. Be rigorous and honest; note that C5 was NOT reproduced (numerical coarse converged fine here).
